title: Technology competition with China
text:
Yes, I agree with Friedman's take on our recent history with China. /s (short for sarcasm)

Just a reminder for Tom. The last decade, under BOTH GOP and Democrats, has been an escalation of threats and suspicion. 

Trump 1.0 with John Bolton as the perpetual paranoid China hawk, involved threats, sanctions, and the COVID-19 mess, including accusations of the China virus.
Biden largely continued the sanctions and hostility.
Trump 2.0 started with maximum escalatory tariffs of 100%, China retaliated with rare earth restrictions, Trump folded like a cheap shirt, and has since been declaring his highest respect for Xi!
Trump alienated every nation that could have formed an alliance.
We cancelled military exercises with South Korea.
We just announced that we have offensive weapons in outer space!

Are the best AI minds in America going to meet Xi and his team in China next week to solve this issue?  

I posit that the problem is NOT China. We can't get our house in order! The best minds in this country can't even convene an emergency national meeting to discuss this emergency. Shouldn't that be the first step?  China's compute is 10% of the US's, and their military spend is 10% of the US's.

Our current administration is calling this a hoax.

So I agree with Tom, we have "an issue."  But, I don't see anything that acknowledges the reality of our governance structures. What will kill us all (whether AI killer robotsI or a pandemic or nuclear holocaust) will be failure of our leadership AND governance. 

Sorry for my deep skepticism.
